summary: Since a 2023 presidential decree Angola waives visas for tourists from around 98 countries — including the EU, UK, US, China and Japan — for stays of up to 30 days per visit and 90 days per year. Everyone else applies for a pre-approved tourist eVisa collected on arrival, and a yellow fever certificate is required from all travellers.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Angola requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) from all travellers aged 9 months and over, whatever your departure point — it is routinely checked on arrival in Luanda.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present year-round throughout Angola, including Luanda. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

travelInsurance.text: Not formally required for tourists, but medical facilities are limited outside private Luanda clinics — comprehensive cover including medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free entry under the 2023 decree formally requires a return or onward ticket, and airlines check before boarding — carry proof, along with accommodation details.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

proofOfFunds.text: Entry conditions include evidence of sufficient means of subsistence and accommodation; no fixed amount is consistently published — carry booking confirmations and a bank card.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency above USD 10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival, and exporting Angolan kwanzas beyond small amounts is prohibited — change money back before departure.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

notes: Diamonds and other minerals may not be taken out of Angola without an official licence.
Photography of government buildings, ports, airports and military sites is prohibited.

payments.text: In Luanda, cards are widely used — the local Multicaixa network is everywhere and international Visa/Mastercard work at hotels, supermarkets and better restaurants. Outside the capital carry kwanzas in cash, and change money only at banks and official bureaux.

safety.text: Luanda is generally manageable but has significant street crime — keep valuables out of sight and use trusted drivers at night. Roads outside the cities are poor, landmines remain a hazard off marked routes in some rural provinces, and the interior of Cabinda province should be avoided due to a lingering separatist insurgency.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Angola Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September — the dry, cooler cacimbo season — is the best window for Luanda, the coast and inland trips; the rains run roughly October to April.

tips.text: Visa-free entry under the 2023 decree is for tourism only — 30 days per visit and 90 days per calendar year. Border officers expect a return ticket, proof of accommodation and your yellow fever card, so keep all three to hand.
Angola checks yellow fever certificates from every arriving traveller — get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and carry the ICVP card with your passport.
Taking kwanzas out of Angola is prohibited beyond small amounts — spend or reconvert your cash before departure, and only exchange money at banks or licensed bureaux.
Little English is spoken outside upmarket Luanda — a few phrases of Portuguese, or a translation app that works offline, goes a long way.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Angola?
faq.answer: Around 98 nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, China, Japan, most of the Americas and much of Africa — have been visa-exempt for tourism since Angola's 2023 decree, for stays of up to 30 days. Everyone else applies for a pre-approved eVisa via the official SME portal or at an embassy.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Angola visa-free?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days per visit, capped at 90 days per calendar year. For longer stays you need a visa from the SME portal or an Angolan embassy, and tourist visas can generally be extended once for a further 30 days in-country.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Angola?
faq.answer: Yes — Angola requires the certificate from all travellers aged 9 months and over, regardless of where you fly from, and it is routinely checked on arrival in Luanda.

faq.question: How does the Angola eVisa work?
faq.answer: You apply online at smevisa.gov.ao and receive a pre-approval letter, usually within about 3–10 business days. You board with the letter and the visa itself is stamped on arrival at Luanda or another international entry point; the fee is around USD 120 — confirm the exact amount during the application.

faq.question: What documents do I need at the Angolan border?
faq.answer: A passport valid 6 months with two blank pages, your yellow fever certificate, a return or onward ticket, and proof of accommodation and means for the stay — these apply to visa-free and visa-holding travellers alike.
